title: RBAC v2 - fastpath approval matrix & SIEM log contract
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the operational approval matrix for RBAC v2 fastpath flows, the minimum evidence we must attach for automated compliance ingestion, and the SIEM export field contract (compact schema) for Hosted / Dedicated / Private environments. Intended audience: security, infra, SRE, platform, product and solutions engineers.

Background/context:
- RBAC v2 introduces role templates (shape-based) + a fastpath approval flow for low-risk privileges to speed onboarding (target: reduce 60% of manual tickets). Fastpath = auto-approve when preconditions met and evidence artifacts are automatically attached to the user entitlement record.
- SIEM export contract: lightweight event shape that every environment must produce (internal aggregator will enrich).

High-level fastpath rules (proposal):
- Eligible roles: viewer-lite, logs-reader, metrics-reader, model-inspector.
- Disallowed: tenant-admin, infra-billing, kms-key-manager.
- Preconditions (all must be true to auto-approve): user has 2FA enabled, user is in an allowlist per identity provider group (okta: /groups/rbac-fastpath), requester has no previous escalations in 90d, requested tenure < 30 days for trial tenants.
- Evidence auto-attachments: identity assertion snapshot (idp assertion id), recent org membership audit, request justification text, automated risk score (low/medium/high).

Fastpath approval matrix (compact):
- Column keys: role, env_hosted_allowed, env_dedicated_allowed, env_private_allowed, manual_escalation_required, min_evidence
- Example rows (we will maintain canonical CSV in repo):
  viewer-lite, yes, yes, yes, no, [idp_assertion, justification]
  logs-reader, yes, yes, yes, no, [idp_assertion, justification, legal_approval_for_private]
  model-inspector, yes, partial, no, maybe, [idp_assertion, justification, owner_approval]
  tenant-admin, no, no, no, yes, [full-risk-review, manager-approval, sec-approval]

Environment-specific differences and notes:
- Hosted (multi-tenant): strict isolation for sensitive roles. Fastpath allowed for readonly roles only. SIEM export must include tenant_id and bounded PII redaction.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated infra): some privileged roles allowed with additional evidence (sales/SAM signoff). Private (VPC/on-prem): fastpath largely disabled; explicit manual review required for changes that touch key material or network scoping.

SIEM export field contract (minimal event schema):
- event_id: string (UUID)
- ts_iso: string (RFC3339)
- environment: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- tenant_id: string (opaque id)
- actor_id: string (identity provider id)
- actor_roles_before: string[] (comma list)
- actor_roles_after: string[]
- action: string (role_grant|role_revoke|policy_attach|policy_detach|role_update)
- target_role: string
- request_id: string (linked to approval workflow)
- approval_path: string (fastpath|manual|canary)
- evidence_keys: string[] (ids for attached artifacts)
- risk_score: string (low|medium|high)
- source_host: string (service that emitted)
- trace_id: string (optional)
- redacted_fields: string[] (fields redacted)

NOTE: The SIEM schema intentionally minimizes PII. Any raw artifacts (e.g., idp assertions) remain in evidence storage; SIEM only receives references (evidence_keys).

Evidence automation contract (how to wire):
- On role change event, the granting workflow must call evidence-collector service with request_id and list of artifact pointers. Evidence collector will store artifacts in immutable evidence-bucket and return evidence_keys. The role change event published to audit bus must include those keys.
- Proof-of-concept mapping: evidence_keys = [evid-20260301-001, evid-20260301-002].

Policy template (short snippet for Hosted readonly role):
- JSON snippet (for human copy):
  {
    "Version": "2023-10-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["observability:ReadMetrics", "observability:ReadLogs"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*"
      }
    ]
  }

Operational playbook (checklist for implementers):
- [ ] Implement idp group allowlist sync (okta -> rbac-fastpath)
- [ ] Wire evidence-collector API and TTP for immutable storage
- [ ] Update audit-producer to include evidence_keys and new contract fields
- [ ] Add SIEM parser rule (SUM: role_change_v2) and unit tests
- [ ] Prepare runbook for manual escalations (sla: 72h)

Rollout plan and tests:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable hosted fastpath for viewer-lite for 2 internal tenants. Monitor SIEM traces and evidence attachments for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2: open to all hosted tenants, enable audit retention 90 days.
- Phase 3: pilot dedicated customers with opt-in via account team.
- Phase 4: Private mode - tools released but default manual.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical evidence storage TTL (immutability window) vs legal retention.
- Clarify mapping for cross-tenant operators (platform SREs) and how to represent in SIEM without leaking tenant mapping.
- Add more granular risk scoring rules (ML-based signals).

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC-4821 (RBAC v2 design doc)
- Jira: JIRA-SIAM-723 (fastpath epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR-1287 (evidence-collector)
- Slack: #sec-ops, #platform-oncall

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; we prefer a compact SIEM contract and evidence key references to avoid PII leakage. Feedback: are the preconditions too lax? Is legal ok with evidence-key-only exports?

Author: Aisha Patel (please comment inline for acceptance criteria and edits).
